slot.brief: Evaluate a limit of the form (1 + a/x)^{bx} or (a^x − b^x)/x reduced to the e-limb standard form; require algebraic rewriting before applying the standard limit.

working:
$\dfrac{12^x-3^x}{x}=3^x\dfrac{4^x-1}{x}$; $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}3^x=1$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{4^x-1}{x}=\ln 4$. Hence the limit is $\ln 4$.

Independent check: Using \(a^x=1+x\ln a+o(x)\), the limit is \(\ln 12-\ln 3=\ln 4\).
solution:
Write $12^x=3^x4^x$, so
$$\frac{12^x-3^x}{x}=3^x\frac{4^x-1}{x}.
$$
As $x\to0$, $3^x\to1$ and $\frac{4^x-1}{x}\to\ln4$; hence the limit is $\ln4$.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses the smaller base alone; C: incorrectly takes $\ln(12-3)$; D: omits the $3^x$ term when differentiating.
